performance_intent: Adds an SSE2 eight-digit char16_t parser in digit_comparison.h
checked_scope: Eight arbitrary char16_t code units, eight validated ASCII decimal digits, guarded accumulator, and one public from_chars<double,char16_t> input with FASTFLOAT_SSE2=1
checker: Bidirectional Alive2 on LLVM IR from exact historical headers; native historical public binaries and UBSan
compiler: Clang 20.1.8 C++20 -O2 -msse2 -DFASTFLOAT_SSE2=1 for IR; GCC 11.4.0 C++20 -O2 -msse2 -DFASTFLOAT_SSE2=1 for public runtime

result.alive2_valid_digits: Both directions refute target_raw_valid; old 76640200 and new 2550200 for one valid eight-digit input in the forward counterexample
result.alive2_guarded: Two guarded parse_if_eight_digits_unrolled outputs prove equal in both directions
result.public_native_sse2: For decimal text 17763508237772000257, both accept and consume 20 char16_t units; old double bits 43eed0951411a402, new bits 43c1b229b788ddfc
result.public_native_default: With FASTFLOAT_SSE2 undefined, both return bits 43eed0951411a402
result.sanitizer: Both SSE2 historical binaries report a common out-of-bounds 16-byte load from an 8-byte static mask array in fast_read_u64<char16_t>

limitations: The IR-level counterexample is real under the compiled LLVM model, but the shared historical source-level out-of-bounds load prevents a defined-C++ public equivalence or inequivalence verdict. The SSE2 path requires explicit FASTFLOAT_SSE2=1 here. No official before/after benchmark score was measured.
